newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia cotton crop still a record - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia cotton crop still a record - ABARE.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) has reduced slightly its forecast of Australia's 1996/97 record cotton harvest to 2.5 million bales or 571,000 tonnes.
The forecast, in ABARE's latest Australian Crop Report, compares with its last forecast of 2.6 million 500 lb bales, or 582,000 tonnes.
The latest forecast production would still set a new Australian record, surpassing the previous record of 2.2 million 500 lb bales in 1991/92.
ABARE said in its latest crop report that the 1996/97 cotton crop had started slowly but ahead of schedule.
"Hot days and cold nights in most areas have slowed plant growth, but in most regions this is not a significant concern," it said.
Recent hail storms had caused negligible crop damage and the small areas of replanting had since recovered well, it said.
Good water allocations and abundant soil moisture in all areas meant that growers would be able to take advantage of warmer weather to assist crop growth, it said.
Total cotton plantings are forecast to increase by 28 percent to a record 388,000 hectares for 1996/97, with 316,000 hectares irrigated and 72,000 hectares dryland, it said.
